name: restsharp/RestSharp
description: Evaluation questions for RestSharp, a lightweight C# HTTP API client library wrapping HttpClient. Held-out C# corpus written from reading the real source in eval_repos/restsharp, independent of RepoGuide's C# semantic provider implementation -- not tuned against provider output.

questions.question: How does RestSharp model pluggable request authentication?
questions.expectedAnswer: Through the `IAuthenticator` interface (a single async `Authenticate(IRestClient, RestRequest, CancellationToken)` method). `AuthenticatorBase` is an abstract base class implementing it, handling the common apply-a-header pattern via an abstract `GetAuthenticationParameter` hook. Concrete authenticators (`HttpBasicAuthenticator`, `JwtAuthenticator`, the OAuth1/OAuth2 authenticators) each override that hook. An authenticator is attached via `RestClientOptions.Authenticator`.

questions.question: RestClient.cs is only part of the RestClient class's own source -- what's going on there?
questions.expectedAnswer: `RestClient` is declared `partial`, split across multiple files (`RestClient.cs` for construction/disposal, plus other `RestClient.*.cs` files such as `RestClient.Async.cs`) that all contribute members to the same logical class. This is a real, common C# pattern for splitting a large type across files, linked via `<DependentUpon>` in the project file.

questions.question: What are the `[GenerateImmutable]` and `[GenerateClone]` attributes on RestClientOptions, and where do they come from?
questions.expectedAnswer: They're markers consumed by RestSharp's own custom incremental source generators (in `gen/SourceGenerator/`), not part of the C# language or BCL. `[GenerateImmutable]` generates a read-only wrapper type (`ReadOnlyRestClientOptions`) from the mutable `RestClientOptions`; `[GenerateClone]` generates a static factory method to copy properties between related types (e.g. from `RestResponse` into `RestResponse<T>`).

questions.question: Where is the RestClient class defined?
questions.expectedAnswer: In `src/RestSharp/RestClient.cs` (a partial class, also extended by other `RestClient.*.cs` files in the same directory).

questions.question: Which file defines the RestRequest class?
Where is the IAuthenticator interface declared?
Which class implements the shared logic for authenticators, leaving only the credential-specific header value to subclasses?
Where is the mutable client configuration class (base of the generated read-only options wrapper) defined?
Trace what happens when you construct `new HttpBasicAuthenticator(username, password)` (the 2-argument overload).
questions.expectedAnswer: The 2-argument constructor delegates via `: this(username, password, Encoding.UTF8)` to the 3-argument primary constructor, which (as part of its own base-call) invokes `AuthenticatorBase(GetHeader(username, password, encoding))` -- `GetHeader` base64-encodes `username:password` into the Basic-auth header value, which becomes `AuthenticatorBase`'s stored `Token`.

expectedFlow.description: Overload delegation into a primary constructor, which itself feeds a computed value into the base class's primary constructor.

questions.question: How does AuthenticatorBase.Authenticate actually attach credentials to a request?
questions.expectedAnswer: `Authenticate` calls the abstract `GetAuthenticationParameter(Token)` (overridden per concrete authenticator -- e.g. `HttpBasicAuthenticator` returns a `HeaderParameter` with a `Basic <token>` value) and adds whatever `Parameter` it returns onto the request via `request.AddOrUpdateParameter(...)`.

expectedFlow.description: Template method in the base class calling an abstract hook overridden by each concrete authenticator.

questions.question: RestRequest has 3 constructors -- how do they relate to each other?
questions.expectedAnswer: `RestRequest(Uri resource, Method method)` delegates via `: this(...)` to `RestRequest(string? resource, Method method)`, converting the URI to its absolute (or original) string form first. That string-based constructor itself delegates via `: this()` to the parameterless constructor (which just sets `Method = Method.Get`) before parsing any query string out of the resource and adding it as query parameters.

expectedFlow.description: Three-deep constructor delegation chain: Uri overload -> string overload -> parameterless overload.

questions.question: RestClient has many overloaded public constructors -- what's the actual entry point they all funnel down to?
questions.expectedAnswer: The constructors taking a `string`/`Uri`/`ConfigureRestClient` all delegate via `: this(...)` down to the primary constructor taking `(RestClientOptions options, ConfigureHeaders? configureDefaultHeaders, ConfigureSerialization? configureSerialization, bool useClientFactory)`, which does the real work: configuring serializers, wrapping the options, and building or reusing the underlying `HttpClient` depending on `useClientFactory`. A separate pair of constructors accepts a caller-supplied `HttpClient` directly instead of building one.

expectedFlow.description: Convenience constructor overloads all funneling into one primary constructor that does the real setup work.

questions.question: Explain AuthenticatorBase's structure -- what does the primary constructor do, and what does Authenticate do?
questions.expectedAnswer: The primary constructor parameter `token` is stored into the `Token` property, which subclasses can update later (it has a `set`). `Authenticate` is an expression-bodied async method: it awaits the abstract `GetAuthenticationParameter(Token)` hook and adds whatever parameter it returns onto the request -- the entire class is a small template-method pattern with one hook left to subclasses.

questions.question: Walk through what RestRequest's string-resource constructor does with the resource string.
questions.expectedAnswer: It delegates to the parameterless constructor first (`: this()`, setting the default `Method`), stores the resource and method, and returns early if the resource is blank. Otherwise it looks for a `?` marking a query string; if one exists (and there's a real `key=value` pair after it), it parses the query string into key/value pairs with a local function (`ParseQuery`), strips the query string off `Resource`, and adds each parsed pair as a query parameter on the request.

questions.question: What does RestClient.ConfigureHttpMessageHandler configure on the HttpClientHandler, and why is so much of it wrapped in `#if NET`?
questions.expectedAnswer: It disables cookie handling and auto-redirects (RestClient manages both itself), applies credentials/decompression/pre-authentication settings and client certificates from `RestClientOptions`, and sets up a proxy if supported. Several checks (`OperatingSystem.IsBrowser()`, `IsIOS()`, `IsTvOS()`) are wrapped in `#if NET` because those APIs only exist on the modern `net8.0`+ target frameworks -- RestSharp also multi-targets older frameworks (`netstandard2.0`, `net471`, `net48`) that don't have them, so the checks are conditionally compiled out on those targets.

questions.question: Where does RestSharp implement a GraphQL query executor?
questions.expectedAnswer: It doesn't -- RestSharp is a REST/HTTP client library; it has no GraphQL-specific query building or execution anywhere in its source.

questions.question: Does RestSharp include a built-in ORM for persisting deserialized response objects to a database?
questions.expectedAnswer: No. RestSharp's serializers (`ISerializer`/`IDeserializer`) only convert between HTTP bodies and .NET objects (JSON/XML/CSV); persisting those objects to a database is entirely outside its scope.

questions.question: What Kafka or RabbitMQ integration does RestSharp provide for queuing failed requests for retry?
questions.expectedAnswer: None -- RestSharp has no message-queue integration of any kind. Retry/resilience behavior isn't built into RestSharp itself; users typically compose it with a separate library (like Polly) around the underlying HttpClient if they need that.

questions.question: I just edited RestClient.cs locally but haven't reindexed. Which class does it define, and could the index be stale for it?
questions.expectedAnswer: It defines the `RestClient` class (a partial class -- other `RestClient.*.cs` files contribute additional members), in `src/RestSharp/RestClient.cs`. Since that file was just modified without reindexing, any cached understanding of it (including this answer) may be stale or dirty and should be re-verified against the current file contents.
